finding_key: packages/backend/src/analytics/analytics-warehouse.service.ts::hand-rolled sql literal escaping reinvents `mysql2`'s own escaper, which is already imported in this file
evidence: Verified against analytics-warehouse.service.ts: line 3 imports 'mysql2/promise' (used for createPool), and lines 33–44 define a hand-rolled sql() escaper handling only backslashes and quotes. mysql2/promise does re-export SqlString's escape/format (also pool.escape()), which handles the full escape set (\0, \n, \r, \x1a, ") the bespoke helper omits. The diff also confirms the maintenance-cost point: the original quote-only escaper had to be patched this round to add backslash handling plus dedicated tests. The finding is real but is a maintainability/design-fit issue, not a live correctness bug, since the fixed escaper is adequate for the document-id and date values it escapes.
